findings.explanation: The Cisco Intersight Add-on for Splunk publishes a fixed set of sourcetypes: alarms, auditrecords, compute, fabric, network, networkelements, profiles, pools, targets, contracts, advisories, licenses, metrics, custom:inventory and custom:metrics. There is no `firmwarerunningfirmware`, `computephysicalsummary`, `hclstatus`, `firmwaredistributable` or `firmwarepolicy` sourcetype.
findings.quote: each Intersight class maps to a lowercased sourcetype prefix `cisco:intersight` plus the MO name without dots
findings.suggested_fix: Explain that running-firmware data comes from a custom inventory input (sourcetype `cisco:intersight:custom:inventory`, filtered on `ObjectType="firmware.RunningFirmware"`) or from whichever add-on sourcetype carries it. Use `cisco:intersight:compute` for model and serial.

findings.explanation: firmware.RunningFirmware exposes Component, PackageVersion, Type and Version, plus relationships to BiosUnit, ManagementController, StorageController, StoragePhysicalDisk, NetworkElements, PciSwitch, GraphicsCard and RegisteredDevice. It has no `Server` relationship and no `Mode` property. The server join key described here does not exist.
findings.quote: The FirmwareRunningFirmware stream carries nested relationship objects: Server.Moid, Server.Name, and Component, Version, Mode, and PackageVersion matter for joins.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the owning server from `Ancestors`/`Parent` or `RegisteredDevice.Moid`, after confirming the shape in a raw event.

findings.explanation: The stanza scheme and the `mo_class_filter`/`sourcetype_prefix` keys are presented as reference config but are not documented add-on settings. The passwords.conf example (`[credential::...]` with `api_key_id`/`secret_key`) is not valid passwords.conf syntax either. Readers will copy these.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the invented stanzas and point readers to the add-on's Configuration and Inputs pages (account plus inventory/custom inventory input), as described in the Cisco Intersight Add-on user guide.

findings.explanation: `Component` describes the image kind (boot-loader, system, kernel), and the hardware class is in `Type`. The sample CSV keys BIOS and BMC rows on `component`, so those rows never match the lookup.
findings.quote: normalise component labels to match the Component or Type you see in firmwarerunningfirmware (examples: system, BIOS, BMC, IOM, adapter, storage-controller, disk)
findings.suggested_fix: Key the baseline on `Type` (hardware class) plus `Component` (image kind), using values taken from real events.

findings.explanation: `_indextime` is not a valid timestamp source field. Overriding the add-on's own sourcetype parsing with INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS and TRUNCATE=0 is risky, and it is presented without reference to how the add-on already parses its data.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the props override and rely on the add-on's shipped parsing. Add search-time FIELDALIAS only where needed.

findings.explanation: The detection compares a running-firmware snapshot with a lookup. It is not a Change event, and it never uses the Inventory data model. No cimSpl backs either claim.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave cimModels empty unless a CIM-mapped search path is actually provided.

findings.explanation: Sibling UC-19.1.19 states 1000 requests per hour for the same API. Neither figure is sourced.
findings.quote: plan for roughly 100 requests per minute per account as a design guardrail
findings.suggested_fix: Cite Cisco's published Intersight API rate limits and use the same value in both UCs.

findings.explanation: Cisco's B-Series blade line appears to end at B200 M6, with X-Series succeeding it. The CSV row `UCSB-B200-M7` and the FI 6332 version string `9.3(5)I43(7c)` also look invented.
findings.quote: Cisco UCS B200 M5 through M7 blades
findings.suggested_fix: Check the B-Series model list and the FI firmware version strings against Cisco data sheets and release notes, and remove any model or version that does not exist.

findings.explanation: Redis has nothing to do with Intersight firmware compliance.
The sourcetype and join key do not exist in the product, so the search cannot have been verified against real data.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until the search is validated against live add-on data.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `sourcetype="cisco:intersight:firmwarerunningfirmware"` and `cisco:intersight:computephysicalsummary` are not sourcetypes published by the Cisco Intersight Add-on for Splunk, so the base search and the join subsearch both return nothing.

`server_moid = coalesce('Server.Moid', server_moid, ServerMoid, parent_moid)` reads fields that firmware.RunningFirmware does not have. `server_moid` is therefore null, and `stats ... by server_moid, server_name, component` drops every event.

`sort +severity_bucket` sorts alphabetically (critical, high, low, medium), not by severity. `hcl_outdated` is computed from the lookup's end_of_support_date, not from HCL status, so the name is misleading.
Check that the drilldown pattern `https://www.intersight.com/an/operate/server/<moid>/inventory/system` is a valid Intersight UI deep link.

summary: A long, confident implementation built on invented plumbing. The Cisco Intersight add-on does not publish per-class sourcetypes such as `cisco:intersight:firmwarerunningfirmware`. firmware.RunningFirmware has no `Server` relationship, so the `server_moid` key the SPL groups on is always null. The inputs.conf, props.conf and passwords.conf examples use made-up keys.
